updates.title: Claude Haiku 5.5 lowers the cost of high-volume agent work
updates.whatChanged: Anthropic introduced Claude Haiku 5.5 for high-volume, cost-sensitive tasks, including summarization, subagents, customer support, and browser use. Anthropic says it is its fastest small model and costs about 75% less to run on average than Haiku 4.5. It adds adjustable effort settings. Anthropic also halved Sonnet 5.5 cache-read pricing from $0.20 to $0.10 per million tokens, which it estimates reduces the cost of most agentic Sonnet work by about 20%.
updates.whyCare: A lower-cost, faster model tier can make delegation of narrow, repetitive tasks more economical, while cheaper cache reads change the cost of repeated-context agent workloads. These are material routing inputs, but vendor claims need validation on enterprise tasks.
updates.before: Teams could use Haiku 4.5 for cheaper requests and reserve stronger models for complex tasks, with cost and capability tradeoffs between tiers.
updates.after: Haiku 5.5 offers a newer option for high-volume tasks at a vendor-reported average 75% lower run cost than Haiku 4.5. Anthropic says it offers best value for prompts up to 100,000 tokens, and it is available through Anthropic and major cloud platforms.
updates.learn: Evaluate cost per successful task, not token price alone. Test effort settings and route bounded subtasks separately from complex work; verify quality, latency, safety, and total agent-run cost against incumbent and competing models.
updates.architectureImplication: Add Haiku 5.5 as a candidate low-cost tier for validated, narrow agent tasks rather than replacing stronger models wholesale. Compare end-to-end success, latency, cache behavior, and safety across providers before changing routing.

updates.title: LangChain reports lower coding-agent costs from task-aware model routing
updates.whatChanged: On October 9, LangChain described a router in its Open SWE coding agent that classifies the initial request and selects a fast, balanced, or performance model tier for the whole thread. In a 973-thread A/B test against always using GPT-6 Astra, median routed-thread cost was $0.94 versus $2.61, a 64% reduction. The merged-PR rates were 29.2% for routed threads and 27.3% for the control (p = 0.49), so the experiment did not establish a quality difference.
updates.whyCare: The report provides production evidence that routing decisions informed by an agent's task mix can reduce spend compared with sending every request to a frontier model. Its measurements are specific to one coding agent and should not be generalized without local evaluation.
updates.before: Open SWE sent all threads to its top-tier model, regardless of task complexity.
updates.after: The agent classifies each initial request and selects among models from multiple providers; the selected model remains in use for the full thread.
updates.learn: Use production traces to characterize task mix, then test routing against a fixed-model control using task success, cost, and user outcomes. A non-significant result is not proof of equivalent quality, and this implementation does not reroute when a thread changes scope.

sources.name: LangChain - How to Build a Model Router in the Harness

updates.architectureImplication: Keep task-specific routing in the agent harness when it depends on the request, tools, and domain context; A/B test it against a strong fixed-model baseline and retain a path for escalation or mid-thread rerouting.
